newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA - GOVERNMENT SAYS IMF PLEASED WITH REFORMS.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA - GOVERNMENT SAYS IMF PLEASED WITH REFORMS.

text.p: The Lithuanian government said on Monday that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) had expressed satisfaction with the direction of the Baltic state's economic reforms.

"The head of a visiting IMF mission, Julian Berengaut, said during a meeting with Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius that the main economic directions and financial results in Lithuania are right," the government's press office said in a statement.
It also quoted Berengaut as saying that the government was "decisively carrying out liberal economic reforms."
The statement added that the IMF urged the government to quicken the pace of privatisation and to eliminate the problems that remain from last year's crisis in the banking sector.
The IMF mission is in Lithuania to assess the country's performance under its memorandum with the fund.
